PullRequest.Title: chat: log a Welcome graphic trigger with multiple editor windows open
PullRequest.Body:

This PR adds an experiment trigger to the Agents window graphic on the Welcome page (`chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic`). When the graphic could be seen while more than one editor window is open, the page now also logs `experimentTrigger` with the `treatmentName` `config.chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic.multipleEditorWindows`.

Only in that case does `auto` show a different graphic than `windowComparison`: it shows `manyWindowsToOne`. With the new trigger, an analysis can compare the setting's values in just these cases. It is logged the same way for every value of the setting, including `none`, so it doesn't depend on which graphic is shown.

Nothing changes in what users see.

Tracking: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10431

**Implementation**
- `AgentsWindowGraphic` now counts the open editor windows whenever the setting changes, for every value instead of only for `auto`, and exposes the result as `hasMultipleEditorWindows`.
  - `auto` still picks its graphic from this count, so the trigger is logged exactly when `auto` shows `manyWindowsToOne`. The other values ignore the count.
  - For values other than `auto`, this adds one `IHostService.getWindows` call when the Welcome page creates the graphic.
- `createAgentsBanner` logs the new trigger at the same moment as the `config.chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic` trigger: when the Agents window section is visible and the page shows its categories. It waits until the windows have been counted and there is more than one editor window.
  - As before, the Agents window doesn't count as an editor window, and each trigger is logged once per window.
- The trigger name follows the `config.<setting>.<key>` form of keyed experiment triggers. It is exported as `AGENTS_WINDOW_GRAPHIC_MULTIPLE_EDITOR_WINDOWS_TREATMENT`.
- The Component Explorer fixture passes the new option.

**How to test**
1. Run Code OSS from sources. Make sure that the Welcome page shows the Agents window section: the Agents window is available and AI features and agent mode are enabled.
2. Set `"chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic": "none"` and run **Developer: Show Telemetry**.
3. Open a second editor window with **File > New Window**, then open **Help > Welcome** in either window. The Telemetry output logs `telemetry/experimentTrigger` with `config.chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic` and then with `config.chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic.multipleEditorWindows`.
4. Close the second window, reload the window and open the Welcome page again. Only `config.chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic` is logged. An open Agents window doesn't count as an editor window.
5. Repeat with `windowComparison`, `manyWindowsToOne` and `auto`. The new trigger is logged in the same cases. While a graphic is shown, `config.chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowSectionStyle` is also logged, as before.

**Validation**
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentSessionsBanner.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentsWindowGraphic.test.ts`: passed, 40 passing.
  - New tests cover every value of the setting with 1 editor window, with 2 editor windows, and with 1 editor window plus the Agents window. They also cover a window count that arrives after the section is shown.
  - When the windows are counted only for `auto`, as before this change, 6 of these tests fail.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- ESLint on the 6 changed files (`node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js --max-warnings 0 <files>`): passed.
- `pnpm run precommit` (hygiene): passed.
- I didn't run the How to test steps in a dev build.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed guard, constructor call from `buildCategoriesSlide`, banner visibility gate, and Electron `ProxyChannel` implementation were traced directly. The exact IPC duration varies by platform and window count, but its new reachability and eager placement are explicit and tests assert the increased request counts.
Findings.PerformanceResource: renderer-to-main-process IPC calls plus allocation and serialization of metadata for every open editor window
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One new IPC occurs per `AgentsWindowGraphic` construction and per graphic-setting change in each non-auto arm; each response does O(open editor windows) mapping/serialization, and page rebuilds or multiple editor windows create additional calls, with in-flight calls not cancelled on disposal.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive IPC and avoidable main-process/renderer work
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Only the `Auto` variant enumerated windows because its rendered design depended on the count; fixed variants and `None` rendered without any `getWindows` boundary call.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Constructing `AgentsWindowGraphic` and every graphic-setting change now starts editor-window enumeration for every variant instead of only when `Auto` needs the result.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: At RIGHT line 86 the previous `Auto` guard is replaced by an unconditional `variant.read(reader)`, so the unchanged async `countEditorWindows(...)` call below is now reached for `None`, `WindowComparison`, and `ManyWindowsToOne` as well as `Auto`.
Findings.Title: Defer telemetry-only window enumeration until banner exposure
Findings.Impact: Opening or rebuilding the Welcome page now performs unnecessary renderer/main-process IPC and main-process window-list serialization in all non-auto experiment arms, including when AI/agent mode hides the banner and no trigger can be logged. This adds avoidable work to a common startup surface and multiplies across Welcome-page instances or rebuilds.
Findings.Evidence: `GettingStartedPage.buildCategoriesSlide` always constructs `AgentsWindowGraphic` before `createAgentsBanner` determines whether the banner is visible. The autorun now calls `countEditorWindows`, whose `hostService.getWindows({ includeAuxiliaryWindows: false })` delegates through `NativeHostService`'s `ProxyChannel` to the Electron main process; the main-process handler maps every open main window and returns all metadata. The updated test demonstrates one request even for `None` and a new request on every variant change.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the existing eager count only for `Auto`; for fixed/none variants, start and coalesce the count when `visible && isExposed` first becomes true (or otherwise activate it lazily from the banner), so hidden/unavailable banners and category rebuilds do not issue telemetry-only IPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or rebuild the Welcome page in a non-auto arm, including when the Agents banner is unavailable or not exposed.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Welcome page and fixed graphic render without awaiting the new count, so this IPC is off the visual critical path; the telemetry-only result matters only after the banner is visible and exposed. It nevertheless competes with startup/main-process work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Electron renderer requests the full main-window list through the native-host `ProxyChannel`; main process maps and serializes metadata for all open windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per `AgentsWindowGraphic` construction and per graphic-setting change; the returned payload contains one record per open main window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No window-list IPC occurred for `None`, `WindowComparison`, or `ManyWindowsToOne`; only `Auto` requested it because design selection required the result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by fixed/none rendering and not required before the page progresses; it is eager telemetry-only work in these arms.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Records a deduplicated experiment-trigger telemetry event for later telemetry transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one new event per telemetry service/window for the multiple-editor-windows treatment, and only when multiple editor windows are found.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This treatment event was not recorded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The call is synchronous into the telemetry service but bounded and not awaited; downstream upload is outside page progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of Welcome-page/graphic instances and rebuilds or setting changes, multiplied by the number of open editor windows serialized per request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each graphic instance owns an independent autorun with no shared limiter or request coalescing. Disposal prevents committing stale results but does not cancel in-flight IPC, so overlapping instances/rebuilds can overlap requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache or coalescing for editor-window counts: every graphic construction and relevant configuration event starts a fresh request, including warm Welcome-page rebuilds. Experiment telemetry is deduplicated per telemetry service/treatment by `loggedTreatments`.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the removed variant guard, unconditional async call, eager page construction, Electron IPC proxy, and O(window-count) main-process mapping are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Main-process IPC latency and the number/frequency of Welcome-page rebuilds vary, and browser builds enumerate locally; severity is low because each request is bounded and not awaited by fixed rendering.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity eager-work regression: the diff introduces avoidable full-window-list IPC before the telemetry trigger can be reachable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Welcome page with the `Auto` graphic variant and multiple editor windows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For `Auto`, window enumeration must complete before the graphic design becomes known and renders; this critical-path dependency predates the PR. The added experiment event runs only after visibility/exposure and count completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerates editor windows to select `manyWindowsToOne` versus `windowComparison`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-window-list IPC per `Auto` graphic construction or setting run, returning O(open main windows).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same call selected the `Auto` design before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks selection/rendering of the automatic graphic, but this placement and cardinality are pre-existing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Records the new deduplicated experiment trigger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one new treatment event per telemetry service when more than one editor window is open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not block graphic rendering or page progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Open main-window count for IPC payload; telemetry cardinality remains one per treatment/window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One uncancelled request per instance/configuration run, as before for `Auto`; no diff-introduced increase in call cardinality for this arm.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No window-count cache is used; each `Auto` graphic instance/configuration change recounts as before. The new telemetry treatment remains once-per-window deduplicated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the auto call path and telemetry deduplication were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry pipeline cost is implementation-dependent, but strict once-per-window deduplication bounds it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding: the expensive count is pre-existing and required for rendering, while the new telemetry event is bounded to one.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change the graphic setting or rebuild the categories slide while Welcome is open.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Setting changes synchronously rerun the autorun and launch asynchronous enumeration; page interaction does not await it, though `Auto` rendering waits for the current result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-enumerates all main windows after every graphic-setting event regardless of whether the variant uses the count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC per setting change per live graphic and one per rebuilt graphic, each serializing O(open windows).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changes among non-auto variants performed no enumeration; transitions into `Auto` alone started a request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Usually off the interaction critical path for fixed variants; obsolete in-flight calls still consume renderer/main-process resources.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of setting events/rebuilds and concurrent Welcome-page instances, with O(open windows) response work each time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rapid setting changes can leave multiple IPCs in flight because requests are not cancelled or sequenced; Welcome-page walkthrough rebuilds are throttled, but each completed rebuild creates a fresh graphic/request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Window counts are neither cached nor shared. Autorun disposal suppresses stale writes only; it does not cancel the underlying request. Telemetry remains deduplicated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the observable dependency reruns on setting changes and no cancellation reaches the IPC operation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users rarely change this experiment-controlled setting rapidly, and walkthrough-driven rebuild frequency varies, which limits severity rather than changing the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: This reinforces the reported eager-work finding; no separate finding is needed because it is the same unconditional enumeration mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files. One low-severity eager IPC regression was submitted; the new telemetry event itself is once-per-window deduplicated, and the `Auto` variant's critical-path enumeration is pre-existing.
